To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spike protein of the murine coronaviruses can be studied on the virus-like particles, and that cleavage is not a prerequisite for infectivity.
the spike protein of murine coronavirus MHV-A59 induces virus-to-cell fusion and that this function of the spike can be studied on VLPs.

the function of the spike (S) protein of the murine coronaviruses can be studied in virus-like particles (S protein is required for VLP infectivity) and that cleavage of S is not required for MHV-A59 VLP infectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system in which the function of S can be studied in detail.

the development of a new system to investigate the function of the spike glycoprotein of coronaviruses and the development of a system in which the function of cleaved and uncleaved spike proteins can be studied.
the identification of domains of the spike protein that are essential for virus infectivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the function of the spike glycoprotein of MHV-A 59 can be studied with VLPs.
the spike protein of murine coronavirus strain A59 is not required to mediate infectivity, as has been suggested for other viruses.
the spike protein of coronavirus MHV-A59 has a function in virus entry that is independent of the cleavable S1/S2 domain and that is mediated by S1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S of MHV-A 59 is a functional protein, which can be studied in VLPs.
VLP infectivity is mediated by S in an M- and E-dependent manner.
the spike protein of the murine virus MHV-A59 can be used for studying virus-to-cell fusion, syncytium formation, and viral infectivity on VLPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the system described here can be used to study the function of S and other viral proteins of MHV-A 59 and other coronaviruses.
VLPs are a useful tool for studying the function of the S protein of MHV.
VLPs are a useful tool to study the function of the S protein in MHV-A59.
